one_sentence: This document argues that physics describes a specific adversarial intelligence that strategically aims entropy, decoherence, and decay to destroy coherence.
executive_summary: This document synthesizes seven domains of physics—thermodynamics, quantum decoherence, radioactive decay, information theory, force ranges, product structure, and closed systems—to argue that the properties of entropy, decay, and decoherence collectively describe a strategic, intelligent adversary rather than mere mindless processes. Key evidence includes the optimal attack ordering (truth first, covenant second, faith last) derived from the product structure of χ, the short-range nature of decay forces (10⁻¹⁸ meters) versus infinite-range grace, and the thermodynamic cost of lies. The conclusion is that the adversary can win locally but cannot permanently win in any open system, as grace, truth, and love have structural advantages that favor redemption.
short_summary: This document is a physics-based analysis of the adversary's character using entropy, decoherence, decay, information theory, force ranges, product structure, and closed systems. The core structural claim is that the adversary strategically aims entropy and decay in an optimal sequence to destroy coherence. Key evidence includes the computational test showing truth-first attack ordering and the asymmetry between short-range decay and infinite-range grace. This matters because it shows the fight is real but structurally tilted toward redemption.
